newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan consumer spending recovering, tone weak--EPA.
newsitem.headline: Japan consumer spending recovering, tone weak--EPA.

text.p: Japan's consumer spending is still on a recovery track, but the weak tone of the recovery is likely to continue, a senior official at the government's Economic Planning Agency (EPA) told reporters on Tuesday.
Earlier, the EPA announced that Japan's household spending for August was unchanged year-on-year at an average of 327,623 yen per household.
Household spending failed to rise in August on a year-on-year basis because of a nationwide food poisoning epidemic in the summer, the official said.
"If we discount the effects of the food poisoning, consumer spending is recovering, but it is still weak," he said.
In August, spending on durable goods such as cars and personal computers rose 26.7 percent in real terms, while spending on non-durable goods such as food fell 2.5 percent, he added.
